problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)=5{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$

feedback.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -15 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =-3,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}=5.
$$
